propositions.name: absolute_time_flows_equably
propositions.statement: Absolute time, of itself and from its own nature, flows equably without regard to anything external.
propositions.quote: Absolute, true, and mathematical time, of itself, and from its own nature flows equably without regard to anything external, and by another name is called duration

propositions.name: duration_independent_of_motion
propositions.statement: The duration of the existence of things remains the same whether motions are swift, slow, or none at all.
propositions.quote: The duration or perseverance of the existence of things remains the same, whether the motions are swift or slow, or none at all

propositions.name: no_equable_motion_may_exist
propositions.statement: There may be no equable motion in nature, yet the progress of absolute time is liable to no change.
propositions.quote: It may be, that there is no such thing as an equable motion, whereby time may be accurately measured. All motions may be accelerated and retarded, but the true, or equable, progress of absolute time is liable to no change.

propositions.name: absolute_space_immovable
propositions.statement: Absolute space, in its own nature, remains always similar and immovable.
propositions.quote: Absolute space, in its own nature, without regard to anything external, remains always similar and immovable.

propositions.name: immovable_places_from_infinity
propositions.statement: Immovable places are those which, from infinity to infinity, retain the same given position one to another.
propositions.quote: Now no other places are immovable but those that, from infinity to infinity, do all retain the same given position one to another; and upon this account must ever remain unmoved; and do thereby constitute immovable space.

propositions.name: order_of_parts_immutable
propositions.statement: The order of the parts of time is immutable, and so also is the order of the parts of space.
propositions.quote: As the order of the parts of time is immutable, so also is the order of the parts of space.

propositions.name: absolute_motion_translation_between_places
propositions.statement: Absolute motion is the translation of a body from one absolute place into another.
propositions.quote: Absolute motion is the translation of a body from one absolute place into another; and relative motion, the translation from one relative place into another.

propositions.name: definite_fact_of_real_rest
propositions.statement: Real, absolute rest is the continuance of a body in the same part of immovable space.
propositions.quote: But real, absolute rest, is the continuance of the body in the same part of that immovable space, in which the ship itself, its cavity, and all that it contains, is moved.

propositions.name: velocities_combine_by_addition
propositions.statement: True motions and relative motions combine by simple arithmetic addition and subtraction across parts, ship, and earth.
propositions.quote: then the sailor will be moved truly in immovable space towards the east, with a velocity of 10001 parts, and relatively on the earth towards the west, with a velocity of 9 of those parts.

propositions.name: simultaneity_at_one_time
propositions.statement: A body's occupation of parts of absolute space is well-defined at one time and at another time without ambiguity of observer.
propositions.quote: will at one time be one part of the absolute space into which the air passes; at another time it will be another part of the same

propositions.name: motion_of_whole_sum_of_parts
propositions.statement: The motion of the whole is the same thing with the sum of the motions of the parts.
propositions.quote: The motion of the whole is the same thing with the sum of the motions of the parts; that is, the translation of the whole, out of its place, is the same thing with the sum of the translations of the parts out of their places

propositions.name: quantity_matter_from_density_and_bulk
propositions.statement: The quantity of matter arises from density and bulk conjunctly.
propositions.quote: The quantity of matter is the measure of the same, arising from its density and bulk conjunctly.

propositions.name: mass_proportional_to_weight
propositions.statement: The quantity of matter of a body is proportional to its weight, as found by pendulum experiments.
propositions.quote: And the same is known by the weight of each body; for it is proportional to the weight, as I have found by experiments on pendulums, very accurately made

propositions.name: quantity_of_motion_from_velocity_and_matter
propositions.statement: The quantity of motion arises from the velocity and the quantity of matter conjunctly.
propositions.quote: The quantity of motion is the measure of the same, arising from the velocity and quantity of matter conjunctly.

propositions.name: body_persists_in_rest_or_right_line
propositions.statement: Every body endeavours to persevere in its present state of rest or of moving uniformly forward in a right line.
propositions.quote: endeavours to persevere in its present state, whether it be of rest, or of moving uniformly forward in a right line.

propositions.name: right_line_uniform_motion_meaningful
propositions.statement: A body without impressed force would fly off in a right line with uniform motion.
propositions.quote: were it not for the opposition of a contrary force which restrains them to, and detains them in their orbits, which I therefore call centripetal, would fly off in right lines, with an uniform motion.

propositions.name: true_motion_only_altered_by_force
propositions.statement: True motion is neither generated nor altered but by some force impressed upon the body moved.
propositions.quote: True motion is neither generated nor altered, but by some force impressed upon the body moved; but relative motion may be generated or altered without any force impressed upon the body.

propositions.name: gravity_accelerates_all_bodies_equally
propositions.statement: At equal distances from the earth, gravity equally accelerates all falling bodies, whether heavy or light, great or small.
propositions.quote: at equal distances, it is the same everywhere; because (taking away, or allowing for, the resistance of the air), it equally accelerates all falling bodies, whether heavy or light, great or small.

propositions.name: motive_force_sums_from_accelerative
propositions.statement: The motive force of a whole body is the sum of the actions of the accelerative force upon its several parts.
propositions.quote: For the sum of the actions of the accelerative force, upon the several articles of the body, is the motive force of the whole.

propositions.name: circular_motion_yields_recession_forces
propositions.statement: Absolute circular motion produces forces of receding from the axis; purely relative circular motion does not.
propositions.quote: For there are no such forces in a circular motion purely relative, but in a true and absolute circular motion, they are greater or less, according to the quantity of the motion.

propositions.name: bucket_water_ascent_reveals_rotation
propositions.statement: The ascent of the water toward the sides of the vessel proves its true circular motion and measures its endeavour to recede from the axis.
propositions.quote: This ascent of the water shows its endeavour to recede from the axis of its motion; and the true and absolute circular motion of the water, which is here directly contrary to the relative, discovers itself, and may be measured by this endeavour.

propositions.name: cord_tension_measures_globe_rotation
propositions.statement: The tension of a cord connecting two revolved globes discloses their absolute circular motion.
propositions.quote: we might, from the tension of the cord, discover the endeavour of the globes to recede from the axis of their motion, and from thence we might compute the quantity of their circular motions.

propositions.name: rotation_detectable_in_immense_vacuum
propositions.statement: The quantity and determination of circular motion can be found even in an immense vacuum with nothing external or sensible for comparison.
propositions.quote: And thus we might find both the quantity and the determination of this circular motion, even in an immense vacuum, where there was nothing external or sensible with which the globes could be compared.

propositions.name: true_rest_bodies_rest_mutually
propositions.statement: Bodies really at rest do rest in respect to one another; change of relative position never happens between bodies truly at rest.
propositions.quote: For they change their position one to another (which never happens to bodies truly at rest)

propositions.name: remote_body_may_be_at_absolute_rest
propositions.statement: In the remote regions of the fixed stars, or perhaps beyond them, there may be some body absolutely at rest.
propositions.quote: in the remote regions of the fixed stars, or perhaps far beyond them, there may be some body absolutely at rest

propositions.name: surrounding_motion_transferred_to_contained
propositions.statement: Bodies relatively at rest within surrounding bodies partake of the motions of those surrounding bodies.
propositions.quote: Therefore, if surrounding bodies are moved, those that are relatively at rest within them, will partake of their motion.

propositions.name: natural_days_unequal_correctable
propositions.statement: The natural days are truly unequal, and astronomers must correct this inequality to obtain absolute time.
propositions.quote: For the natural days are truly unequal, though they are commonly considered as equal, and used for a measure of time; astronomers correct this inequality for their more accurate deducing of the celestial motions.

propositions.name: astronomical_equation_yields_true_time
propositions.statement: The astronomical equation, evinced by pendulum clocks and Jupiter satellite eclipses, is necessary for determining the times of a phenomenon.
propositions.quote: The necessity of which equation, for determining the times of a phenomenon, is evinced as well from the experiments of the pendulum clock, as by eclipses of the satellites of Jupiter .

propositions.name: one_real_circular_motion_per_body
propositions.statement: There is only one real circular motion of any one revolving body, corresponding to only one power of endeavouring to recede from its axis.
propositions.quote: There is only one real circular motion of any one revolving body, corresponding to only one power of endeavouring to recede from its axis of motion, as its proper and adequate effect

propositions.name: projectile_could_orbit_earth
propositions.statement: A projectile with sufficient velocity would revolve in an orbit and go round the whole earth, or proceed in its motion in infinitum.
propositions.quote: or lastly, so that it might never fall to the earth, but go forward into the celestial spaces, and proceed in its motion in infinitum .

propositions.name: moon_retained_by_force_toward_earth
propositions.statement: The moon must be drawn aside toward the earth by some force of just quantity, else it could not be retained in its orbit.
propositions.quote: If this force was too small, it would not sufficiently turn the moon out of a rectilinear course: if it was too great, it would turn it too much, and draw down the moon from its orbit towards the earth.

propositions.name: impressed_force_only_acts_during_action
propositions.statement: An impressed force consists in the action only and remains no longer in the body when the action is over.
propositions.quote: This force consists in the action only; and remains no longer in the body, when the action is over. For a body maintains every new state it acquires, by its vis inertiæ only.
